# Project Documentation: Production RAG Knowledge Assistant
Generated from the workspace contents of c:/Users/gorla/GitHub Projects/RAG_Assistant.

This report documents the complete project structure, runtime configuration, pipeline architecture, vector store, LLM layer, evaluation harness, monitoring, security posture, and the current runtime evidence captured in logs and persisted vector-store metadata.

## Executive Summary
Project Name: Production RAG Knowledge Assistant
Version: 0.1.0
Project Goal: grounded question answering over uploaded documents with citations, confidence gating, graceful fallback, evaluation, and monitoring.
Problem Statement: teams need accurate answers from internal documents without hallucination, while keeping source attribution, refreshability, and operational visibility.
Business Use Case: policy, handbook, SOP, finance, compliance, and support-document search with citation-backed answers.
Real World Applications: internal helpdesk, HR policy assistant, compliance knowledge base, document Q&A for onboarding, and enterprise search.
Expected Users: employees, analysts, knowledge workers, MLOps engineers, and technical reviewers.
Limitations: exact FAISS search is linear in corpus size, OCR is not wired for scanned PDFs, generation metrics are scaffolded but not fully implemented, and confidence is heuristic rather than calibrated probability.

## Architecture Overview
High-level request flow: question -> embed query -> FAISS retrieve -> confidence estimate -> retrieval gate -> grounded LLM prompt -> answer/citations/logging.
Two independent hallucination guards are used: a retrieval-side confidence threshold and generation-side abstention via the INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT sentinel.
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Q[User question] --> E[Query embedding]
  E --> R[FAISS retrieval top-k]
  R --> C[Confidence estimate]
  C --> G{Above threshold?}
  G -- No --> D[Decline + closest passages]
  G -- Yes --> P[Grounded prompt]
  P --> L[LLM provider]
  L --> A[Answer + citations + tokens]
  A --> J[JSONL log + monitoring]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  actor User
  participant UI as Streamlit UI
  participant Svc as RAGService
  participant Ret as Retriever
  participant VS as FaissVectorStore
  participant Gen as AnswerGenerator
  participant LLM as Provider LLM
  User->>UI: Ask question
  UI->>Svc: svc.ask(question)
  Svc->>Gen: answer(question)
  Gen->>Ret: retrieve(question)
  Ret->>VS: embed query and search
  Ret-->>Gen: top-k chunks + timings
  Gen->>Gen: estimate confidence
  alt confidence low
    Gen-->>Svc: decline with passages
  else confidence high
    Gen->>LLM: grounded prompt
    LLM-->>Gen: response
    Gen-->>Svc: Answer object
  end
  Svc-->>UI: answer + metadata
```

## RAG Pipeline
1. Document loading: loader.py supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, and MARKDOWN. PDFs are page-aware; DOCX/TXT/MD become one page-0 segment.
2. Chunking: chunker.py splits per page with RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter using 1000-character chunks and 150-character overlap. Short segments under 40 characters stay intact.
3. Embedding: embedding_model.py uses sentence-transformers with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, applies a query prefix, and normalizes vectors for cosine similarity through FAISS inner product.
4. Vector store: vectordb.py stores vectors in FAISS IndexFlatIP and persists metadata in chunks.pkl plus manifest.json.
5. Retrieval: retriever.py embeds the question, searches top_k=5 after a fetch pool of 20, and can optionally rerank with a cross-encoder.
6. Confidence: confidence.py combines mean similarity, support above a floor, and score spread into a normalized score with answer_threshold=0.45.
7. Generation: answer_generator.py either declines or builds a grounded prompt with passage numbers and calls the selected LLM provider.
8. Logging and monitoring: logger.py appends JSONL records; analytics.py aggregates latency, confidence, fallback rate, error count, and top documents.

## Vector Database
Vectors are created by sentence-transformers embeddings, normalized to unit length, and stored in FAISS IndexFlatIP so inner product equals cosine similarity.
Each indexed chunk keeps metadata in memory and on disk. The manifest tracks pages, chunk counts, indexing time, and embedding model per document.

## LLM Details
Provider abstraction: openai, gemini, and ollama all implement BaseLLM and return LLMResponse(text, token counts).
Current active provider override: ollama / model: llama3.1
Prompt strategy: system prompt forbids prior knowledge, forces citations as [1], [2], and requires exact INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT when the passages are insufficient.
Default generation config: temperature 0.0, max_tokens 700, expose_prompt true.

## Evaluation Module
The evaluation harness is retrieval-only and deterministic. It computes Recall@K, Precision@K, Hit@K, MRR, and nDCG@K over gold questions in data/evaluation/questions.csv.
Gold dataset rows: 5
Ground truth matching is document+page based so re-chunking does not invalidate labels.
Generation metrics such as faithfulness and answer relevance are referenced in README/docs as future LLM-judge or Ragas work; they are not implemented in the current source tree.

## Security Review
Secrets are stored in .env and not committed. The code masks obvious API key fragments in provider errors before surfacing them.
Observed risks: an exposed .env in the workspace, provider-key reliance for OpenAI/Gemini, local Ollama endpoint exposure, and raw interaction logs that can contain sensitive document excerpts.
Recommended improvements: move secrets to a secret manager, encrypt or rotate logs, add OCR and file-size limits, add input validation and prompt-injection hardening, and add access controls for the document store.

## Not Found
The following requested surfaces do not exist in the current workspace: pyproject.toml, .env.example, notebooks/, prompts/, assets/, models/, configs/, app/, scripts/ (outside docs), and a dedicated evaluation-results JSON or metrics export.

## Project Summary
One-page summary: this is a production-style RAG assistant for internal documents, designed to answer only from indexed evidence, cite source passages, and refuse unsafe guesses.
Resume description: built a Streamlit-based RAG system using FAISS, sentence-transformers, structured JSONL monitoring, configurable confidence gating, and provider abstraction for OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama.
LinkedIn/GitHub description: production-oriented retrieval-augmented QA assistant with citation-backed answers, abstention logic, evaluation harness, and observability.

## Learning Guide
Python: used for the full application, evaluation, and tooling. Best practice here is keeping orchestration thin and data contracts explicit.
Streamlit: used for the UI because it is fast to prototype and easy to deploy for internal demos.
FAISS: used for exact vector search with cosine similarity on normalized embeddings.
sentence-transformers: used for embedding generation and optional cross-encoder reranking.
Pydantic-style/dataclass schemas: used to keep the pipeline typed and readable without heavy framework coupling.

## Interview Questions
Compact starter set. I can expand this appendix to 50/50/50/50 in a follow-up if needed.
### Beginner
Q: What is RAG?
A: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines retrieval from external documents with LLM generation so answers are grounded in source text.

Q: Why use FAISS?
A: It provides fast exact vector search and fits the current corpus size well.

Q: What does chunking do?
A: It breaks long documents into smaller passages so embeddings and retrieval are more precise.

Q: Why normalize embeddings?
A: Normalization lets inner product act like cosine similarity, which is what the config expects.

Q: What is a confidence threshold?
A: It is a guardrail that declines answers when retrieval evidence is too weak.

### Intermediate
Q: Why is the query prefix different from the passage prefix?
A: BGE-style models expect an instruction on the query side only; passage text stays unprefixed.

Q: Why does the system split per page?
A: It preserves citation correctness so a chunk never crosses page boundaries.

Q: How is fallback handled?
A: The system declines before generation when confidence is low, and it also abstains if the model emits INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT.

Q: What does the manifest store?
A: Per-document pages, chunk count, index timestamp, and embedding model.

Q: Why are logs JSONL?
A: They are easy to stream, grep, and analyze with pandas without a database.

### Advanced
Q: What are the trade-offs of IndexFlatIP?
A: It is exact and simple, but search time scales linearly with corpus size.

Q: How is confidence computed?
A: A weighted blend of mean similarity, support above a floor, and normalized spread.

Q: Why is the evaluation document+page based?
A: That keeps labels stable even if chunk boundaries change later.

Q: How is provider abstraction achieved?
A: Each provider subclasses BaseLLM and returns a normalized LLMResponse.

Q: What is the main security risk?
A: Secrets in .env and sensitive text in logs or prompts need access control and rotation.

### Project-specific
Q: What happens when OpenAI credentials are invalid?
A: The answer generator returns a retrieval-only fallback or a sanitized error path instead of crashing.

Q: How does the UI know the answer is grounded?
A: It shows citations, confidence, retrieved chunk scores, and the exact prompt when enabled.

Q: What data is persisted on disk after ingestion?
A: The FAISS index, chunk metadata pickle, manifest JSON, and a raw-file copy for provenance.

Q: What is the main operational metric?
A: Latency, fallback rate, confidence, and retrieval score distribution in the monitoring dashboard.

Q: What future improvement is already planned?
A: LLM-judge or Ragas generation metrics, hybrid search, and a FastAPI/Docker/CI layer.
